jobs.description:

Description:
Join our Collaborative Care team!

Trinity Health IHA Medical Group is seeking a compassionate and patient-focused Behavioral Health Specialist
to join our Behavioral Health Collaborative Care team. In this role, you'll support patients experiencing behavioral health concerns through assessment, care coordination, brief evidence-based interventions, patient education, and ongoing symptom monitoring that improves outcomes and enhances the patient experience.

What You'll Do:

Support and closely coordinate behavioral health care with primary care providers, psychiatric consultants, and other treating providers

Screen and assess patients for common mental health and substance use disorders

Provide patient education regarding behavioral health conditions and available treatment options

Monitor patients for changes in clinical symptoms, treatment response, and medication side effects through in-person and telehealth interactions

Support psychotropic medication management by promoting treatment adherence and identifying barriers to care.

Deliver brief evidence-based behavioral health interventions such as Behavioral Activation and other structure therapeutic approaches.

Track patient outcomes and document clinical encounters.

What We're Looking For:

EDUCATION: Master’s degree or higher in Social Work, Counseling, or a related behavioral health field from an accredited university.

CREDENTIALS/LICENSURE: Valid Michigan clinical licensure (LMSW, LPC, LMFT, or similar applicable licensure).

MINIMUM EXPERIENCE: Experience assessing and treating common mental health and/or substance use disorders preferred. Experience utilizing evidence-based interventions such as CBT, PST, or Behavioral Activation preferred. Experience working with individuals with co-occurring behavioral and physical health conditions preferred.

Why Join Trinity Health IHA Medical Group?

Day-one benefits with no waiting period for eligible colleagues.

Predictable outpatient schedule with a focus on work-life balance.

Collaborative team environment with strong provider partnerships.

Career growth, development, and advancement opportunities.

Meaningful work improving the health of patients and communities across Southeast Michigan.

At Trinity Health IHA Medical Group, we're committed to delivering exceptional care through our core values of Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, Efficiency, and Service. If you're passionate about patient-centered care and want to make a difference every day, we'd love to have you join our team.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Fairness feels good

Make a real impact at AFCA. Where fairness drives every decision. Help us deliver world-class, independent complaints resolution for Australians. As a not-for-profit and progressive financial ombudsman, we’re championing positive change. Achieving our purpose takes progressive thinking, accountability and resilience. At AFCA, our inclusive leadership values every voice. We offer our people flexible work options, thoughtful benefits and opportunities to deepen expertise. Flourish in a diverse, caring culture. Feel the difference of belonging to an organisation intentionally designed to put people first.

Job Description

At AFCA, fairness means making sure everyone has the opportunity to be heard and access the support they need.

As our Equity of Access, Program Coordinator
, you’ll help keep one of AFCA’s strategic programs organised, connected and moving forward. Working alongside colleagues across program delivery, projects, change and communications, you’ll coordinate meetings, prepare materials, maintain key information and support professional communication with stakeholders.

This is a great opportunity to build practical experience in project coordination, change and stakeholder engagement while contributing to work with a clear social purpose. You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone who is organised, curious, and ready to learn. If you’re passionate about fairness and believe your skills align with this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every single criterion.

This is initially a 12- month contract position.

Typically, In This Role You Will

Provide day-to-day administrative and coordination support across the Equity of Access program.
Coordinate program meetings, including committee, governance forum and external Advisory Board meetings.
Schedule meetings and manage invitations, calendars and supporting arrangements.
Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, papers, packs and presentations.
Take minutes, update action registers and follow up outstanding actions.
Monitor and maintain the program mailbox and calendar.
Keep the Equity of Access SharePoint site accurate and up to date.
Maintain program registers, contact lists, distribution lists and other administrative records.
Work closely with the Program Lead, Project Manager, Change Manager and Senior Communications Advisor to keep program activities moving.
Support clear, timely and professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.
Manage routine tasks, meet agreed timeframes and handle program information confidentially and professionally.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you will need:

Experience in an administrative, coordination, customer service or office support role is advantageous but not necessary, this is an entry level position.
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage routine tasks, follow up actions and meet agreed timeframes.
Interest in Project management, Change management or Stakeholder engagement.
Confidence using Microsoft 365 tools, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint, or willingness to build capability in these tools.
Ability to work collaboratively, ask questions when guidance is required and maintain confidentiality and professionalism when handling programme information.
Can do attitude and interest in learning is essential.

Additional Information

Gold AWEI Accreditation 2025 – Recognised for LGBTQ+ workplace inclusion.
Accredited Family Friendly Workplace – Supporting work-life balance and inclusivity.
Hybrid working – Flexible arrangements with two days a week in our modern offices designed for collaboration and wellbeing.
Additional and inclusive leave options – Flexible public holidays, gender affirmation leave, women’s health leave, and bonus paid time off over the end of year holiday period.

To apply

If you’re passionate about fairness and believe your skills align with this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every single criterion.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, abilities, sexual orientations, and gender identities. If you require any accessibility support during the recruitment process, please reach out to our team at Careers@afca.org.au.

We believe fairness starts with people. That’s why we don’t use AI or automated tools to screen candidates. As a result, our processes may take a little longer, and we thank you for your patience.

About AFCA

The Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) was established in 2018 as a private not-for-profit ombudsman service providing free, fair and independent help with financial disputes. The original team has grown to over 1600 dedicated professionals. Since 2018, AFCA has received more than 634,000 complaints, helping to secure $2.1 billion in compensation for consumers.

AFCA is a 2026 Circle Back Initiative Employer - we are committed to responding to every applicant.

Description:

Serves as the primary coordinator and resource person for obtaining and sustaining designation as an ANCC Magnet™ hospital. Assumes responsibility for coordination of the ANCC Magnet™ application, designation, and re-designation process.

Job Title:
Magnet Program Coordinator

POSITION PURPOSE

Under general supervision, supports the organization in implementation of initiatives related to obtaining and maintaining Magnet™ designation and ensuring the organization's milieu reflects the internalization of the five components of Magnet. Serves as the primary coordinator and resource person for obtaining and sustaining designation as an ANCC Magnet™ hospital. Assumes responsibility for coordination of the ANCC Magnet™ application, designation, and re-designation process. Ensures a well-planned program structure, which addresses Transformational Leadership, Structural Empowerment, Exemplary Professional Practice, and New Knowledge Innovations and Improvements to promote excellence in patient care services as evidenced by Empirical Outcomes.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Accountable for the coordination of the organizational processes to obtain and maintain Magnet designation. Coordinates data collection, management, and analysis to meet Magnet standards toward the submission of the Magnet application. Coordinates and facilitates the organization of the Magnet application process. Writes, and submits interim reports to ANCC. Maintains current understanding, education, and knowledge of Magnet Program standards and updates, and communicates these findings to team members. Collaborates with Magnet experts within and external to Trinity Health. Develops and maintains a core group of Magnet Nurse Champions to collaborate with patient care service leadership team members to assist in education and implementation of the Magnet model. Assists in the development and delivery of Magnet-related education. Mentors staff nurses to support their role as educators about the Magnet process and serves as a resource to the community and area schools of nursing. Serves as an active member of the Magnet Steering Committee and helps to establish a work plan and timeline to achieve and maintain Magnet designation. Maintains and coordinates all internal aspects of Magnet status compliance and initiatives. Creates periodic Magnet journey status reports and presents at various meetings in a variety of settings to a variety of attendees. Serves as a change agent by appropriately challenging current processes, policies, and procedures. Seeks to incorporate new technologies and methods to improve overall effectiveness. Collaborates in the development, implementation and surveillance of nursing initiatives related to professional practice, patient care, and quality.

Demonstrates enthusiasm for the pursuit of nursing excellence and the advancement of professional nursing practice. Maintains a spirit of inquiry utilizing nursing evidence-based practice findings and research methodologies to improve the care delivered. Ability to present unfamiliar detailed information to others in a readily comprehensible way, to work with little direction while being sensitive to issues requiring physician and/or committee involvement, to read, analyze, and interpret professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations, and to write reports, business correspondence, procedures, and policies. Demonstrates outstanding verbal and written communication skills. Demonstrates proficiency with the application of computers in data analysis, use of data based decision-making methodologies.

Other Functions And Responsibilities

Establishes and fosters positive, collaborative, and cooperative relationships with other physicians, nurses, healthcare team members and leadership team members. Maintains the confidentiality of information acquired pertaining to patient, physicians, colleagues, and visitors. Discusses patient and hospital information only among appropriate personnel in appropriately private places. Behaves in accordance with the Code of Conduct, Policies, and the Mission, Vision, and Values. Assumes responsibility for performance of job duties in the safest possible manner, to assure personal safety and that of coworkers, and to report all preventable hazards and unsafe practices immediately to management. Assumes other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Education, Experience And Certification/Licensure

Education
: A Master of Science in Nursing (Clinical, Education, Administration all acceptable)

Experience
: Three years of nursing experience in an acute care setting. Three years of teaching or leadership experience; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

Certification/Licensure
: Current Michigan RN license. A professional board certification accepted by the Magnet Recognition Program must be completed within a year of hire.

Serving as the approachable, enthusiastic adult your K-2 students are excited to see daily

Company Description

Fairness feels good

Make a real impact at AFCA. Where fairness drives every decision. Help us deliver world-class, independent complaints resolution for Australians. As a not-for-profit and progressive financial ombudsman, we’re championing positive change. Achieving our purpose takes progressive thinking, accountability and resilience. At AFCA, our inclusive leadership values every voice. We offer our people flexible work options, thoughtful benefits and opportunities to deepen expertise. Flourish in a diverse, caring culture. Feel the difference of belonging to an organisation intentionally designed to put people first.

Job Description

At AFCA, fairness means making sure everyone has the opportunity to be heard and access the support they need.

As our Equity of Access, Program Coordinator
, you’ll help keep one of AFCA’s strategic programs organised, connected and moving forward. Working alongside colleagues across program delivery, projects, change and communications, you’ll coordinate meetings, prepare materials, maintain key information and support professional communication with stakeholders.

This is a great opportunity to build practical experience in project coordination, change and stakeholder engagement while contributing to work with a clear social purpose. You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone who is organised, curious, and ready to learn. If you’re passionate about fairness and believe your skills align with this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every single criterion.

This is initially a 12- month contract position.

Typically, In This Role You Will

Provide day-to-day administrative and coordination support across the Equity of Access program.
Coordinate program meetings, including committee, governance forum and external Advisory Board meetings.
Schedule meetings and manage invitations, calendars and supporting arrangements.
Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, papers, packs and presentations.
Take minutes, update action registers and follow up outstanding actions.
Monitor and maintain the program mailbox and calendar.
Keep the Equity of Access SharePoint site accurate and up to date.
Maintain program registers, contact lists, distribution lists and other administrative records.
Work closely with the Program Lead, Project Manager, Change Manager and Senior Communications Advisor to keep program activities moving.
Support clear, timely and professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.
Manage routine tasks, meet agreed timeframes and handle program information confidentially and professionally.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you will need:

Experience in an administrative, coordination, customer service or office support role is advantageous but not necessary, this is an entry level position.
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage routine tasks, follow up actions and meet agreed timeframes.
Interest in Project management, Change management or Stakeholder engagement.
Confidence using Microsoft 365 tools, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint, or willingness to build capability in these tools.
Ability to work collaboratively, ask questions when guidance is required and maintain confidentiality and professionalism when handling programme information.
Can do attitude and interest in learning is essential.

Additional Information

Gold AWEI Accreditation 2025 – Recognised for LGBTQ+ workplace inclusion.
Accredited Family Friendly Workplace – Supporting work-life balance and inclusivity.
Hybrid working – Flexible arrangements with two days a week in our modern offices designed for collaboration and wellbeing.
Additional and inclusive leave options – Flexible public holidays, gender affirmation leave, women’s health leave, and bonus paid time off over the end of year holiday period.

To apply

If you’re passionate about fairness and believe your skills align with this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every single criterion.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, abilities, sexual orientations, and gender identities. If you require any accessibility support during the recruitment process, please reach out to our team at Careers@afca.org.au.

We believe fairness starts with people. That’s why we don’t use AI or automated tools to screen candidates. As a result, our processes may take a little longer, and we thank you for your patience.

The original team has grown to over 1600 dedicated professionals. Since 2018, AFCA has received more than 634,000 complaints, helping to secure $2.1 billion in compensation for consumers.
